title: Adapting Safe-for-Work Classifier for Malaysian Language Text: Enhancing Alignment in LLM-Ops Framework
measurement_description: The paper evaluated the ability of language models to identify and classify 'Religious Insult' as part of a broader Safe-for-Work (SFW) content taxonomy. 'Religious Insult' is defined as content that disrespects, mocks, or insults religious beliefs, practices, or figures, including blasphemy and offensive jokes.
base_benchmarks: EXIST: sEXism Identification in Social neTwork (EXIST)
findings: The study successfully curated a dataset and trained a classifier to detect inappropriate content, including 'Religious Insults,' in the Malaysian language. Topic modeling on the dataset revealed that religious insults were primarily aimed at Islam and Christianity, frequently employing terms such as 'islam', 'kristen', 'quran', and 'prophet muhammad'. Among the models evaluated, 'mesolitica/malaysian-mistral-191M-MLM' achieved the highest accuracy (0.8768) and overall performance in identifying harmful content categories.
